observations: Photo 0: a V-type engine with an automatic gearbox still bolted to it, lying on the ground in an open workshop yard, a mechanic bending over it.
Photo 0: the gearbox casing is long and dusty with oil and dirt residue; no transfer case attached at the tail, only an output end.
Photo 0: hoses, wiring and accessories still hang off the engine; a loose bracket lies on the ground at the lower left.
Photo 0: no ID tag, casting number, brand or model text is readable on the gearbox; low resolution.
Photo 0: watermark 'GEARUP IN...', a dealer photo; nothing shows the unit running or being tested.
The photo shows engine and gearbox together, while the seller's words offer a gearbox only.

identity.kind: used automatic gearbox for a V8 pickup truck (shown still attached to the engine)
read_from: photo 0 shape of an automatic gearbox bolted to a V engine; no plate or tag readable

claims.evidence: No ID tag or casting number readable in photo 0. The years given span two truck generations that used different gearboxes, so the fitment itself is unclear.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo; it also sits uneasily with the later 'direct from Belgium'.
Origin cannot be shown remotely, and it conflicts with the seller's own 'Direct America' line.
No test clip or written warranty shown.
Photo 0 shows the unit out of any vehicle on the ground; no clip of it running or shifting.
No clip with sound of the unit running.
A pulled gearbox has no odometer to show.
Casing bolts and pan seals are not shown close up in photo 0.

risks.risk: The gearbox model is unknown; a 4-speed and a 6-speed unit for these trucks differ widely in value and fit, and the stated years cover both.
risks.proof: Close, sharp photo of the gearbox ID tag or the casting number on the casing.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; model needed first

risks.risk: Gearbox slips, fails to shift or has internal wear.
risks.proof: Clip of the gearbox fitted in a vehicle, driving through all gears, with the seller's handwritten note in shot.

risks.risk: Gearbox has been opened or rebuilt, or has burnt fluid.
risks.proof: Close-up of the pan bolts and seals, and a photo of fluid from the dipstick or drain on white paper.

risks.risk: Unclear what is sold: gearbox alone, or engine and gearbox together, and whether the torque converter and a 4x4 transfer case are included.
risks.proof: Photo of exactly the parts being sold laid out separately, torque converter included.
risks.if_unproven: as gearbox only, without torque converter or transfer case

proof_requests: Sharp close-up of the gearbox ID tag or casting number.
Photo of the gearbox alone, separated from the engine, with the torque converter and a handwritten note with today's date.
Clip of the gearbox fitted and driving through all gears.
Close-up of pan bolts and seals plus a fluid sample on white paper.
response.reason: The photo shows an automatic gearbox on a V8 engine but no readable tag, and the seller's years cover two generations with different gearboxes, so the model that sets the price is unknown. The ID tag photo is needed before even a worst-case price.
